title: Year-end governance and priorities - All Hands
summary: Executive update covering end-of-year priorities, a light hiring pause window, governance tweaks for deployments in regulated regions, incident-readiness playbook launch, and people/compensation Q&A. Action items assigned for org leads to follow up with teams; next steps include publishing a short governance FAQ and scheduling follow-ups for benefits and SRE runbooks.
next_steps: Publish short governance FAQ and new deployment checklist (Priya) - target 2026-12-13
Share incident playbook and schedule 90-min SRE tabletop (Lena) - target 2026-12-17
People team to share compensation timeline and Q&A doc (Samira) - target 2026-12-10
Product/Eng to finalize Q1 scope and headcount requests for exec review (Priya + Ethan) - target 2026-12-20
action_items: Priya: Draft governance FAQ + deployment checklist; due 2026-12-13
Lena: Publish incident playbook and set tabletop exercise; due 2026-12-17
Samira: Post compensation Q&A doc and run two office hours; due 2026-12-10
Ethan + Priya: Consolidate headcount asks into single doc; due 2026-12-20
Avery: Send short note to customers about year-end support windows; due 2026-12-08
transcript:
Meeting header:
Date: 2026-12-06
Start: 16:00 UTC
Duration: ~72 minutes
Attendees: Avery, Marcus, Priya, Ethan, Samira, Lena + companywide dial-in

[00:00] Avery: Hey everyone, thanks for joining, uh, quick housekeeping - we'll record, we'll post slides after, and we, uh, want to keep this tight. Year-end all-hands, call it Steadfast Compass.

[00:18] Marcus: Morning/afternoon folks. Real quick agenda -- governance, incidents/readiness, budget/hiring guidance, people updates, then Q&A.

[00:30] Priya: I'll be brief on product priorities, the main ask is alignment so the execs can consolidate Q1 asks. We are focusing on dedicated/private parity and shipping the Optimize improvements that reduce per-token cost.

[00:48] Avery: High level: great year — product shipped, customers expanded — but macro's shifted. We'll be careful on spend and prioritize projects that impact customer SLOs and unit economics. That means a temporary tightening window that is not a full freeze but a review-first posture.

[01:05] Samira: To be transparent: we're implementing a short hiring pause for non-critical roles for the next three weeks to let leadership finalize priorities. This is not a layoff announcement. We'll run reviews with hiring managers; exceptions possible for customer-critical hires.

[01:28] Speaker 7: questions about ramp timing?

[01:33] Ethan: We'll prioritize infrastructure and reliability roles. Eng leads, please flag exceptions into the hiring board. Priya and I will meet with each hiring manager this week.

[01:50] Lena: On reliability — recent trends showed a slight uptick in tail latency during holidays in our EU region, seen in the dashboard. We're rolling a new routing policy that favors capacity regionalization and early fallback to smaller quantized variants. There's a short window to validate before Q1.

[02:12] Marcus: Quick tech note — kernel/compilation improvements the runtime team landed cut median token latency by ~6% on long-context jobs. But the tail still matters; Lena's plan will address outliers.

[02:30] Priya: Governance update: for customers with regulated-data needs, we are tightening the private deployment checklist and adding an explicit KMS/HSM proof path. That means new required docs for on-prem handoffs and an audit-readiness checklist. This will slow some private deployments by a week or two but it's necessary for SOC/ISO asks.

[02:55] Avery: The ask to teams: document any customer engagements that might be affected and let sales and solutions know. We'll be proactive rather than reactive.

[03:10] Samira: People update — compensation cycle: we are planning a limited refresh targeted at performance-critical bands; full company-wide adjustments will follow a compensation review in January. We'll publish the timeline and FAQs.

[03:30] Audience noise / brief crosstalk.

[03:45] Audience Q: Will the hiring pause affect internship offers?

[03:50] Samira: Interns in pipeline are considered mission-critical for recruiting; we will not cancel offers that are already extended, but new intern requisitions will be reviewed.

[04:05] Priya: Product roadmap highlights: 1) Redwood Optimize v2 trials for top ten customers, 2) streaming improvements to reduce token overhead, 3) rollout of per-route dashboards in Console. We're delaying some lower-impact UX initiatives.

[04:35] Ethan: Engineering priorities: secure the EU/regional fallback play, finalize autoscaling burst policies for Dedicated, and stabilize the new batching layer. We'll freeze feature merges for low-priority branches for two weeks to shake down reliability patches.

[05:00] Marcus: There was a question earlier about competitors; nothing super new, but we're watching inference runtime projects from others. Our differentiator remains unified ops and quantization profiles tuned for customers.

[05:20] Avery: Financial note: operating runway remains healthy, but we choose to optimize spend. We will push non-customer-facing capital projects to Q2 unless they materially improve unit economics.

[05:40] Audience chat: applause, emoji reactions.

[06:00] Lena: Incident readiness — we are launching an incident playbook (draft linked in #sre) and a tabletop exercise next week. The playbook includes cross-region fallback, manifest lists for canaries, and a clear escalation ladder. We need all product and infra leads to attend the tabletop.

[06:25] Priya: Note on governance artifacts: new deployment checklist will include encryption at rest verification, network diagrams, and a signed data flow doc. Solutions will get a checklist template.

[06:45] Avery: On customers, we will send a short note to customers summarizing year-end support windows and our maintenance freeze timings. Action for me to send that early next week.

[07:02] Marcus: Small technical aside about model routing: we will enable an automatic fallback to a quantized variant (lower-cost) when longer queues detected; teams should validate quality regressions against their eval sets. Redwood Optimize will suggest thresholds.

[07:25] Audience Q: Any change to hosted pricing?

[07:28] Avery: No immediate change. We'll keep pricing stable and focus on cost reduction for customers through Optimize and batching.

[07:40] Samira: Benefits note — open enrollment reminders: check benefit portal; HR will host two Q&A sessions next Tuesday and Thursday.

[07:58] Priya: On the roadmap we are also prioritizing regulatory-region readiness — that impacts the Private product but also Dedicated (we need to prove data locality controls). Expect a governance FAQ.

[08:25] Audience: question about holiday on-call shifts.

[08:30] Lena: On-call rotations will be tightened; SRE will publish a compact schedule. We'll try to minimize disruption. Expect compensatory time options for holiday shifts.

[08:48] Ethan: Quick ops ask — teams owning long-lived feature branches please rebase; we'll do a batch merge window next week so we can ship critical reliability fixes.

[09:05] Audience: chatter about merge conflicts.

[09:20] Avery: OK open Q&A. Please raise your hand in the Q&A panel; I'll try to answer as many as possible before we run out of time.

[09:35] Staff question (Speaker 11): Are there layoffs planned?

[09:38] Avery: No. This is a real quick pause to get alignment. We are not planning layoffs. If anything changes we'll tell you early.

[09:55] Staff question (Speaker 12): Will the governance changes increase time-to-delivery for Private installs?

[09:59] Priya: Slightly, yes. We added a mandatory KMS proof and an audit checklist. For customers in heavy-regulated industries it's a net positive. Solutions and sales will manage expectations.

[10:20] Staff: question about Q1 priorities.

[10:24] Priya: Q1 is about parity (hosted -> dedicated -> private), Optimize cost improvements, and reliability. We'll publish the Q1 scope doc by Dec 20.

[10:41] Marcus: Another technical note: please check the runtime release notes; we are enabling a beta for 2-stage batching that can cut cost for small prompts.

[10:58] Avery: Final ask — leads: run your 15-min team huddles tomorrow to surface any downstream impacts, then update the priority board. We'll reconvene execs Friday to finalize headcount asks.

[11:15] Samira: Reminding managers to schedule one-on-ones for anyone anxious about changes; HR open office hours and anonymous ask form in the #people channel.

[11:35] Audience: brief applause.

[11:50] Avery: Thanks everyone, we'll post slides, the governance FAQ, and timing for tabletop. Happy holidays in advance.

[12:00] Meeting end.

Notes / Links referenced: governance checklist draft (link in #prod-governance), incident playbook draft (link in #sre), compensation timeline (HR doc), Q1 scope template (link in #roadmap). Some transcription artifacts: speaker labels may be approximate and short timestamps every few minutes.
